text:
katie: Heads-up — CI started failing after the poetry lock regen we ran yesterday. macOS wheel builds for the Rust extension are blowing up.
katie: Error snippet:
```
ERROR: Failed building wheel for rust_token_ext
clang: error: undefined symbol: _Py_buffer_release
Command \"python setup.py bdist_wheel\" failed with exit status 1
```

amar: hmm, that looks like a CPython ABI mismatch — wheels were probably built against a different macOS/Python combo. Could be 3.11 vs 3.12 or different SDK flags. :thinking:

jen: CI link: https://ci.internal.redwood/builds/3201 (job: macos-wheel, linux-wheel)

sam: also seeing a related failure in the KMS integration tests after the lock update — sec-bot reported access denied when unwrapping keys in the e2e job

sec-bot: ALERT: tests/kms_integration::test_signing - AccessDenied: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/team-ops missing kms:Decrypt

amar: suspects: the lock regen changed the build container or the way CI assumes roles. Instance profile or role mapping maybe broken in the new image.

katie: Actionable plan:
- open hotpatch PR to pin rust_token_ext wheel in our constraints so CI can pass
- add a temporary fallback to fetch prebuilt wheel from artifacts bucket
- reproduce locally using manylinux/macos matrix and iterate
- sam to check IAM/KMS perms mapping

jen: I'll take the PR to pin and add test matrix. I'll try to reproduce by running the lock regen inside the official manylinux2014 Docker image.

sam: I'll validate IAM role attachments and the KMS key policy. If team-ops lost kms:Decrypt we'll need infra to reattach or a short-lived key for the test cluster.

ci-bot: Job 3201 failed at 03/20 09:12 UTC — logs uploaded: https://ci.internal.redwood/logs/3201

katie: If upstream can't publish compatible mac wheels quickly, fallback plan is to build wheels ourselves in the manylinux container and upload to S3, then update CI to pull that wheel.

amar: prioritization: this is a compatibility/build issue, not an exploitable CVE. Mark P2, but escalate to P1 if signing/e2e remains red for production flows.

jen: tagging reviewers: @eng-ml @eng-runtime. I'll label PR \"security - dependency\" so it gets quicker eyes.

katie: owners: jen -> dependency patch & regen, sam -> IAM/KMS remediation, amar -> CI reproduction & docker image pin

sam: Quick manual repro command that fixed it for me locally (worked with system headers patched):
```
python -m pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel
pip wheel --no-binary :all: rust_token_ext==1.4.2 --wheel-dir /tmp/wheels
```

jen: good — add that snippet to the PR description and include the S3 fallback steps.

katie: I'll open the hotpatch PR now and include the timeline + rollback instructions. Ping here when CI green or if infra needs to reattach KMS role. :white_check_mark:
